title: Joshua 18
paragraphs: ¹ The whole Israelite community assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land had been brought under their control, ² but there were still seven Israelite tribes who had not yet received their inheritance. ³ Joshua said to the Israelites, How long will you wait before taking possession of the land that the LORD God of your ancestors has given you? ⁴ Appoint three men from each tribe. I will send them out to map the land, making a record of it as it relates to each tribe's inheritance, and they will return to me. ⁵ You are to divide the land into seven portions. Judah is to remain in its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph is to remain in its territory in the north.

⁶ Survey the land and write a description of it in seven sections, then bring it back to me. I will cast lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God. ⁷ The Levites, however, are not to have a portion among you, because the priestly service of the LORD is their inheritance. And Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them. ⁸ The men left and began their survey. Joshua instructed them, Go and walk through the land, map it out, and return to me. Then I will cast lots for you here at Shiloh before the LORD. ⁹ So they went through the land and described it town by town in a scroll, dividing it into seven sections. Then they returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh. ¹⁰ Joshua then cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD and distributed the land to the Israelites according to their tribal divisions.

¹¹ The lot for the tribe of Benjamin came up first. Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Judah and Joseph. ¹² On the north side their boundary began at the Jordan, went up to the ridge north of Jericho, and headed westward into the hill country, ending at the wilderness of Beth Aven. ¹³ From there the boundary went south to Luz — that is, Bethel — and descended to Ataroth Addar near the hill that lies south of Lower Beth Horon. ¹⁴ The boundary then drew a line along the southern slope of the hill opposite Beth Horon and turned southward, ending at Kiriath Baal — that is, Kiriath Jearim — a town belonging to the people of Judah. This was the western side. ¹⁵ The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim, and the boundary went westward to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

¹⁶ The boundary then went down to the foot of the hill facing the Valley of Ben Hinnom, north of the Valley of Rephaim, descended into the Hinnom Valley to the southern slope of the Jebusite ridge, and went down to En Rogel. ¹⁷ It curved north, went out to En Shemesh, then to Geliloth facing the Pass of Adummim, and descended to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben. ¹⁸ It then passed along the northern slope overlooking the Arabah and went down into the Arabah. ¹⁹ The boundary continued along the northern slope of Beth Hoglah and ended at the northern bay of the Dead Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary. ²⁰ The Jordan was the eastern boundary. These were the boundaries on all sides for the clans of Benjamin's inheritance.

²¹ The towns of the tribe of Benjamin by their clans were Jericho, Beth Hoglah, the Valley of Keziz, ²² Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, ²³ Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, ²⁴ Kephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba — twelve towns with their villages. ²⁵ Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,

²⁶ Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah, ²⁷ Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, ²⁸ Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath — fourteen towns with their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Benjamin by its clans.
